scenario: A listener is preparing to buy a first serious pair of headphones and wants mechanism homework rather than another price-tier ranking. They keep seeing wired, Bluetooth, Bluetooth 5.x, Bluetooth Low Energy, LE Audio, A2DP, codec, DAC, amplifier, DSP, and lossless language used as though it all meant the same thing. The available material includes standards-history and protocol pages, audio-coding and playback-chain pages, two current catalog architecture examples, and two community discussions about Bluetooth sound and converting wired IEMs for wireless use.
target: Explain the supported evolution of Bluetooth audio from early standards organization and Classic stereo transport deployment through the Wibree-to-Bluetooth-Low-Energy lineage and the LE Audio and LC3 transition. Then compare the complete wired and wireless playback paths so a first-time buyer can verify the exact endpoints and modes that may create audible differences. Preserve history-versus-deployment, format-versus-implementation, seller-page, and community-experience boundaries; do not manufacture an A2DP release year or a universal wired-better verdict.
